html:
A small Hindu temple of red sandstone near Angkor in Cambodia, consecrated in 967 and dedicated to Shiva. Its carving is the finest in all Khmer art.

Banteay Srei was not built by a king but by Yajnavaraha, a learned courtier and teacher of the future king Jayavarman V, under the Khmer Empire. It lies about 25 km northeast of the main temples. The pink stone is hard but fine grained, and the craftsmen covered doors, walls and gables with leaves, gods and scenes from the Indian epics in deep, crisp relief. The buildings are small, with doors so low an adult must stoop.

The name means citadel of women, a later name perhaps from its delicate carving or from the female figures on its walls. In 1923 the young French writer André Malraux was arrested for cutting out four of those figures to sell. In the 1930s it became the first temple at Angkor restored by taking it apart and rebuilding it with its own stones. It is two centuries older than Angkor Wat.
sum: A small Hindu temple of red sandstone near Angkor in Cambodia, consecrated in 967 and dedicated to Shiva. Its carving is the finest in all Khmer art.
